why: A 24-garage tyre and exhaust chain taking about EUR 1.5 million a month (roughly EUR 62,000 per garage) with a slowly falling margin index as rubber rises is believable.
A new zoo collecting 4,200 visitor questionnaires in April, with both pies adding to 100%, is believable.
A mattress market of about $27 billion today split across spring, foam and hybrid types, growing modestly, is a believable market size.
Cosmetics firms with 24 to 32 skincare products earning 5 to 19 million in skincare profit are believable.
A premium whisky exporter holding 0.2% to 6.6% of spirits sales in ten export countries at margins of 14% to 41% is within the range a distiller could report.
A supermarket chain handling about 1.8 million checkout transactions a month (a few dozen stores) with a steadily narrowing self-checkout funnel is believable.
A mobile studio with twelve games earning $2 to $26 million each and 9 to 48 developers per game (up to about $600,000 revenue per developer) is believable, even while unprofitable.
Shipping lines growing containers 0.9% to 5.7% a year, with driver shares that always sum to 100% and a negative ship-call share where calls fell, are consistent and believable.
A 25-adviser round-the-clock broadband support line hearing from 70,000 customers a year (a couple of hundred calls a day) is believable.
Mobile and fixed-line profits add to the stated totals each year, and the implied sales of about 800 to 1,200 million at 1% to 3.5% margins are low for a telecom but within a stylised range.
